title: Rabbi Elazar bar Yeshitah
author: Aharon Hyman

paragraphs: So it is cited in Otzar Yisrael from Jerusalem Talmud Megillah 4:10. Hyman says, with respect, that it erred in the plain sense of the Jerusalem Talmud, which says there that Rabbi Pedat (son of Rabbi Elazar) was Rabbi Yasa’s amora (spokesman): for teachings he had heard from his father, he would say, “Thus said Rabbi in the name of Father”; for teachings he had not heard from his father, he would say, “Thus said Rabbi in the name of Rabbi Elazar” (for Rabbi Elazar was Rabbi Assi’s teacher). Afterward the Gemara cites, “Bar Yeshita was Rabbi Abbahu’s amora.” Hyman says Otzar Yisrael misread the Jerusalem Talmud and thought that there is an Amora named Rabbi Elazar bar Yeshitah.

notes.text: The heading represents a sage entry that Hyman rejects through his reading of the spokesman/father formulas. His criticism is explicitly attributed. The supplied ד״א is understood contextually as Rabbi Elazar; no new Elazar bar Yeshitah person is admitted.

Guggenheimer Megillah 4:10 directly names Pedat as Yasa’s spokesman and contrasts Father with Rabbi Elazar. Its following Bar Yashita is Rabbi Acha’s spokesman and uses Father/Rabbi Chinna, whereas Hyman supplies Rabbi Abbahu. Preserve the distinction: this witness supports the spokesman formula, not Hyman’s exact Abbahu wording or the uninspected Otzar Yisrael claim, and admits no Elazar bar Yeshitah identity.
